The small block is released from rest from point A at height h on a track with inclination angle $\theta_{1}$, and when it moves to point B its velocity is $v_{1}$. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left side is a horizontal track, and point B is on the horizontal track; on the right side there is an inclined track extending from the horizontal track upward to the right. Point A is located on the inclined track, and the vertical height from A to point C on the horizontal line directly below it is marked h. The figure shows two inclined tracks with different inclination angles: the steeper inclination angle is θ1, the gentler inclination angle is θ2, and θ2<θ1; the contact point between the inclined track and the horizontal track moves along the horizontal line as the inclination angle changes, and there are marks such as D in the schematic. The problem asks to compare the velocities of the block when it reaches point B after being released from rest from point A at the same height h. Reasoning: According to the problem, the coefficient of kinetic friction between the small block and the horizontal track and inclined track is the same; let it be μ. Let the fixed horizontal distance from C to B be L, namely CB=L. For any one experiment, if the inclination angle of the inclined plane is θ, then the length of the inclined plane from point A to the bottom end of the inclined plane is h/sinθ, and the normal force on the inclined plane is mg cosθ, so the magnitude of the friction force on the inclined plane is μmg cosθ. The magnitude of the work done by friction on the inclined plane is μmg cosθ·h/sinθ=μmgh cotθ. The horizontal distance from the bottom end of the inclined plane to C is h cotθ, therefore the horizontal distance from the bottom end of the inclined plane to B is L-h cotθ. The magnitude of the friction force on the horizontal track is μmg, and the magnitude of the work done by horizontal friction is μmg(L-h cotθ). The total magnitude of the friction work in the two segments is μmgh cotθ+μmg(L-h cotθ)=μmgL, independent of the inclination angle θ. The height dropped by the block from A to B is h in both cases, the work done by gravity is mgh in both cases, and the problem states that the mechanical energy loss at the track contact is neglected. Therefore, by the work-energy theorem, the kinetic energy at point B satisfies 1/2 mv^2=mgh-μmgL. This expression is independent of θ, so the velocities reaching point B in the two experiments are the same.
